correctness.rationale: One-intermediate-vertex shortest-path change equals adjacent-position swap of coordinate permutations. The proof exhausts every two-fault coordinate orbit of Q4, separately verifies zero/one fault, and inducts for n>=5. Each permitted first-letter fiber reduces to a <=2-fault instance in dimension n-1 and is connected. Suffix counting excludes at most 2/(n-2)<1 of suffix orders for every first-letter pair whose two-element prefix is not forbidden. The first-letter bridge graph is K_(n-r) with <=2-r edges removed, connected for n>=5. Q3 witness two isolated paths. Both implementations passed their own exhaustive checks; these computations certify base and tests, not the infinite induction.

originality.rationale: The exact arbitrary-two-fault connectivity theorem and sharp dimension threshold were not identified in the accessible literature, indexed published mathematical findings, or readable historical claim statements. The strongest applicable published results establish the unfaulted permutohedral graph and shortest rerouting, and an earlier accessible theorem treats one forbidden internal vertex only. These do not imply two-fault robustness. One-fault connectivity is logically insufficient, as removing an additional vertex can disconnect a configuration graph. Unindexed or stronger unpublished equivalence remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalence of Boolean-lattice diamond-connected maximal chains after two forbidden elements cannot be excluded.
Accessible 2013 and 2024 general-algorithm abstracts were not reviewed at theorem/appendix level; neither is decisive positive coverage on the evidence read.
A stronger general theorem from outside the indexed sources could subsume the result; absent a documented implication, originality is best-knowledge rather than independently certified.

value.rationale: A canonical n-dimensional network retains reachability among all minimum-hop routes under ANY two failed intermediate nodes, with a sharp Q3 boundary. Unlike ordinary fault-tolerant connectivity, this is connectivity of the full optimum-route configuration space under single-node changes. The proof isolates exactly why n>=5 bridges always exist and supplies the finite n4 threshold. It is a meaningful infinite structural robustness result rather than a routine count.
